theme: The crucifixion, “Father, forgive them”; the burial
readingInstruction: Read Luke 23:26-56. The road to the cross, the crucifixion, two criminals, the death of Jesus, and his burial. This is the center of the Gospel. Read slowly and in silence if you can.
settingTheScene: Jesus is led out of Jerusalem to a place called The Skull, carrying his cross, and a bystander, Simon of Cyrene, is forced to carry it for him. A great crowd follows, including women who mourn. Luke’s account is marked by mercy. Even on the cross, Jesus forgives his killers and promises paradise to a dying criminal.
observation: “Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children” (23:28).
“Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do” (23:34).
“He saved others; let him save himself, if he is the Christ of God, his Chosen One!” (23:35).
“Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom” (23:42).
“Truly, I say to you, today you will be with me in paradise” (23:43).
“And the curtain of the temple was torn in two” (23:45).
“Father, into your hands I commit my spirit!” (23:46).
“Now there was a man named Joseph… a good and righteous man” (23:50).
interpretation:
On the way, Jesus turns to the weeping women and tells them to weep for themselves and for their children. He is thinking of Jerusalem’s coming judgment. Even on his way to die, he cares for others.

At the cross, they crucify him between two criminals. His first words in Luke’s account are a prayer: “Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.” This is the opposite of what any of us would pray. The soldiers divide his garments by lot, the rulers sneer, the soldiers mock him, and a sign over his head reads, “This is the King of the Jews.” The mockers say, “Save yourself.” They don’t realize that he is saving others precisely by not saving himself.

One criminal joins the mockery. The other rebukes him: “Do you not fear God?” He acknowledges that they are justly condemned, but this man has done nothing wrong. Then he says, “Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom.” This is faith in its barest form. He has no good works, no time to be baptized, and no way to make amends. He asks only to be remembered. And Jesus answers, “Today you will be with me in paradise.” This is the gospel in a sentence: salvation by grace through faith, immediately, for a dying thief.

Darkness covers the land for three hours, and the curtain of the temple tears in two. The way into the presence of God is now open through the death of Jesus. Then he cries with a loud voice, “Father, into your hands I commit my spirit!” He quotes Psalm 31:5, which you prayed on Day 619, and breathes his last. He does not lose his life. He gives it. The centurion praises God and says, “Certainly this man was innocent!” The crowds go home beating their breasts.

Joseph of Arimathea, a member of the council who had not consented to the plan, asks for the body and lays it in a new tomb. The women from Galilee see where it is laid, prepare spices, and rest on the Sabbath according to the commandment. The body is in the tomb. Everything depends on what happens next.
connection: Isaiah 53:4-12 describes the servant who bore our griefs, was numbered with the transgressors, and made intercession. Psalm 22 begins with the cry of forsakenness and ends in praise. Psalm 31:5 is the prayer Jesus prays. Exodus 26:31-33 describes the curtain before the Holy of Holies. Hebrews 10:19-22 says we have confidence to enter the holy places by the blood of Jesus. Romans 5:8 shows his love for sinners. Acts 7:60 has Stephen echoing the prayer for forgiveness.
application:
Sit with the cross for ten minutes in silence. Do not rush to the resurrection.

Pray the thief’s prayer: “Jesus, remember me.” It is enough.

Forgive someone as Jesus forgave. If you can’t yet, ask him for the willingness.
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for praying, “Father, forgive them,” and ask him to forgive you.
Pray the thief’s prayer: “Jesus, remember me.”
Thank him for the promise of paradise.
